learningObjectives: Distinguish Requirement criteria from structured test data and executable TestCases.
Explain why planned data variation can reduce redundant tests without guaranteeing defect coverage.
Describe how linking and recalculation support current Requirement reporting.
Find the independent Quilyn lessons covering test design topics.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Where TDS1 fits in the testing lifecycle

elements.text: Independent Quilyn introduction based on Tosca On-Premises 2026.1 documentation. The Academy video requires authentication and was not reviewed; this is not a transcript or verified outline of that course.

elements.description: Define expected functional and non-functional behavior with stakeholders, then organize criteria and prioritize business risk.

Plan logical tests and data variation before execution. TestSheets organize Attributes or Steps, Instances hold concrete variations, and Classes support reuse. Templates can instantiate executable TestCases from the design.
Requirements express expected behavior. A TestSheet structures data and processes; an executable TestCase performs checks. These artifacts are related but are not interchangeable.

bulletPoints: Use section names as the reliable identifiers rather than relying only on interface colors.
Design and implementation can evolve together; Tosca does not require every design decision before any executable test is built.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Why invest time up front in test design

elements.description: Select a combination method for the risks and interactions under test. All combinations expands the full defined dataset; Orthogonal covers each value, Pairwise covers value pairs, and Linear expansion varies one non-StraightThrough value at a time around a baseline.

elements.text: Fewer combinations are not evidence of complete defect coverage. Independent example: testing each discount and shipping option separately can miss a defect that occurs only when two options interact.

elements.description: Link executable tests to their Requirements. After changes, Requirement values need recalculation: AutoCalculateRequirements is off by default in 2026.1. Use Update Outdated Values, or enable automatic calculation and restart Tosca; large repositories can incur delays.

bulletPoints: A clear test focus helps diagnosis but cannot guarantee that a failing test has only one possible cause.
Links provide traceability; fresh calculated values and execution results are still necessary for current reporting.

elements.title: Independent local lessons
items: Lesson 1 — Requirements: Folders, RequirementSets, Requirements, and risk weighting.
Lesson 2 — Attributes: structuring a TestSheet with Administration/Precondition/Process/Verification.
Lesson 4 — Combinatorial Methods: All Combinations, Orthogonal, Pairwise, and Linear Expansion.
Lesson 5 — TestCase Specifications: filling in TestSheet values efficiently.
Lesson 6 — Classes: reusing Attribute structures across TestSheets.
Lesson 7 — Link to Requirements: connecting TestCase Design back to the Requirements dashboard.
Lesson 8 — Integration of New Attributes: adapting a TestSheet when the SUT changes.
Lesson 9 — Best Practices: readability, reuse, and Agile (Given-When-Then) structuring.
Lesson 10 — Automatic Generation of Instances: letting Tosca generate combinations for you.

examPitfalls.title: Design versus execution
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A logical data model alone does not execute checks against the application.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Separate criteria, data combinations and executable TestCases; use templates where appropriate to connect design to execution.

examPitfalls.title: Coverage versus quantity
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A small dataset or clear test name does not prove that every defect can be found.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Choose combinations for the required interactions and risk; reducing redundancy is a goal, not a universal minimum-test guarantee.

examPitfalls.title: Stale linked reporting
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Linking a test does not ensure displayed Requirement values immediately reflect later changes.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Check recalculation settings and use Update Outdated Values before reporting.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which two Tosca sections define expected criteria and organize logical test data?
practiceQuiz.hint: Separate criteria and logical design from executable checks.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Requirements define criteria and risk priorities; TestCase-Design organizes logical tests and data variation. The question is about those responsibilities, not an unverified Academy syllabus.

optionExplanations.A: Executable tests and their runs are different from criteria and logical data design.
optionExplanations.B: Requirements supply criteria; TestCase-Design models test data and logical coverage.
optionExplanations.C: Modules represent automation building blocks rather than the two responsibilities asked here.
optionExplanations.D: Data design alone does not replace explicit Requirement criteria.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why invest in structured TestCase-Design before repeating regression runs?

options.text: Execution time increases proportionally, since more TestCases are created.
To reduce redundant variation and select tests for the required coverage, without guaranteeing fewer tests in every project.
Nothing changes in execution; design time is purely additional overhead.

practiceQuiz.hint: Consider targeted coverage and repeated execution effort.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Structured design helps target variation and avoid redundant checks. The chosen method and risks determine the dataset; more design does not automatically guarantee reduced execution time.

optionExplanations.A: More design does not imply proportionally more execution.
optionExplanations.B: Targeted variation can reduce redundancy; the result depends on the risks and method.
optionExplanations.C: Planning affects the chosen tests and is not necessarily unrelated overhead.
optionExplanations.D: Systematic data design does not remove business-risk prioritization.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In Tosca 2026.1, what is needed for linked Requirements to show current calculated values after test changes?

options.text: Manually updating a spreadsheet alongside Tosca.
Link tests to their Requirements and recalculate values manually, or enable AutoCalculateRequirements and restart Tosca.
Requirements are dashboards by default and require no linking.
Only the ExecutionList section can show project status.

practiceQuiz.hint: Traceability and recalculation are separate requirements.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Links associate tests with criteria; calculation refreshes the displayed values. Automatic Requirement calculation is off by default, so linking alone does not ensure a live report.

optionExplanations.A: A separate spreadsheet does not refresh Tosca values.
optionExplanations.B: Correct links plus recalculation support current calculated reporting.
optionExplanations.C: Criteria without linked tests do not show those tests’ coverage.
optionExplanations.D: Requirements also support reporting when tests are linked and values are recalculated.

quickRecap.value: Logical structure, data variation and template-based generation.
Choose coverage of values, pairs or baseline variations for the relevant risks; fewer tests alone do not prove completeness.
Link tests and recalculate Requirement values. AutoCalculateRequirements is off by default in 2026.1.
